bull_bear.title: Non-obvious takeaways

bull_bear.body:
- Recognised global player in drying and process equipment with 8,000+ installations and machines worldwide across 50+ countries on six continents, giving scale and reference credibility in customised process solutions.
- Leadership position in the carbon black segment, plus a proven track record in critical oil & gas and nuclear applications including offshore skid-mounted packages and heavy water drying systems — high-specification niches with steep qualification barriers.
- Integrated technology platform combining drying, thermal and RF technologies after the acquisitions of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, unlocking cross-selling and end-to-end solutions a single-technology competitor cannot offer.
- R&D moat: a Centre of Excellence at Kilburn, Saravali with seven pilot plant dryers for real-world simulation and process validation, plus a Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune, reducing execution risk and improving enquiry-to-order conversion.
- Global technology tie-ups with Nara Machinery (Japan), Komline Sanderson (USA) and Idreco (Switzerland), providing access to advanced technologies and alignment with global standards.
- Material versatility across aluminium, carbon steel, stainless steel, nickel, Inconel, Hastelloy, Monel, duplex stainless steel, alloy steels and titanium, enabling participation in critical, high-performance applications.
- Diversified sectoral presence across 20+ industries, which strengthens resilience and mitigates concentration risk.
- End-to-end execution capability with engineering, fabrication, assembly and testing under one roof across six manufacturing facilities, supporting turnkey and balance-of-plant delivery.
- Order-backed business model with revenue visibility from a diversified order book and an active enquiry pipeline.
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Project execution and input cost pressure on long-cycle orders — Long project execution cycles may expose the Company to input cost fluctuations and margin pressures. Because the business is order-backed and equipment is highly customised, a fixed-price order booked today can be delivered against materially different raw-material costs. Management relies on prudent procurement practices, vendor partnerships, commercial safeguards and close project monitoring.
- Demand cyclicality and working capital strain — Industrial investment cycles, customer-led delivery deferments and payment delays may impact revenue visibility and cash flows. This is structural for a capital-goods supplier whose revenue depends on customers' own capex decisions; mitigation is diversification across industries and geographies, disciplined credit management and active customer engagement.
- Technology replication and intellectual property erosion — The Company's differentiation rests on proprietary drying, thermal and RF process know-how. Risks arise from technology replication and evolving customer requirements, addressed through continuous investment in innovation, engineering and product development.
- Intensifying competition from domestic and international players — Increasing competition from domestic and international players could pressure pricing and win rates; management mitigates through proven technologies, strong execution capabilities, customised solutions and long-standing customer relationships.
- Foreign exchange exposure from export operations — Export operations across 50+ countries expose the Company to currency fluctuations. A structured foreign exchange risk management framework and appropriate hedging strategies are used to mitigate this exposure.
- Macroeconomic, geopolitical and supply-chain disruption — Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions may affect business operations. Mitigation rests on a diversified customer base, multiple sourcing channels and robust project planning processes. The MD&A also notes global growth moderating and trade volumes projected to slow, with tariff-related uncertainties weighing on merchandise exports.
- Integration and execution risk from recent acquisitions — FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield. The growth thesis depends on realising cross-selling, integrated solutions and broader end-market participation from these acquisitions; the platform's scale and complexity require continued investment in engineering capability, leadership depth and project management to keep organisational capacity abreast of growth.
- Sector concentration in process-industry capex — Although the Company serves 20+ industries, demand is uniformly tied to the industrial capex cycle across chemicals, petrochemicals, carbon black, fertilisers and metals, so a broad slowdown in process-industry investment would affect most end markets simultaneously. Diversified sectoral presence is management's stated mitigation against concentration risk.

business.body: The Group designs, engineers and manufactures highly specialised process equipment and systems for critical industrial applications, spanning customised industrial drying systems, packaged process systems, fabricated large critical equipment, waste heat recovery and thermal systems, Radio Frequency (RF) heating and drying, and precision manufacturing. It offers end-to-end design, manufacturing, supply, installation and commissioning, serving more than 20 industrial sectors including carbon black, chemicals, petrochemicals, fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, tea, oil & gas, nuclear power and food processing. outlook.title: Growth verticals / optionality

outlook.body:
- Evolve over the next three to five years from a specialised drying-equipment company into a diversified industrial technology and engineering platform built on four complementary engines: process engineering, energy efficiency, advanced drying and RF technologies, and precision manufacturing.
- Keep process engineering at the core of growth by deepening application expertise and integrated engineering capabilities to address more complex requirements and deliver greater value across the project lifecycle.
- Build energy efficiency into a major growth avenue via thermal engineering and waste heat recovery capabilities that help customers improve energy utilisation and reduce resource consumption.
- Broaden the technology portfolio and addressable market through advanced drying and RF technologies, leveraging the Monga Strayfield integration alongside established drying expertise.
- Scale precision manufacturing as the foundation for delivering increasingly complex and customised equipment with greater consistency, quality and efficiency.
- Move towards higher-value, more integrated multi-technology solutions and unlock cross-selling across existing customer relationships following the integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield.
- Expand the international footprint as customers seek reliable engineering partners with specialised process expertise and proven execution capabilities.
- Expand into high-growth adjacencies including energy efficiency, waste heat recovery, sludge treatment, biomass processing, waste-to-energy, industrial decarbonisation and advanced material processing.
- Invest in organisational capacity — engineering capabilities, leadership depth, project management excellence and digital tools — so the organisation can scale while preserving agility and customer-centricity.
- Convert pipeline strength into profitable delivery while maintaining discipline in margins, capital deployment and performance, through an order-backed business model with strong execution control.
- Sustain an innovation-led approach anchored by the R&D Centre at Saravali and the Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune, using pilot-led validation to accelerate commercialisation and improve enquiry-to-order conversion.
- Prioritise enhancing execution throughput, deepening customer engagement, accelerating innovation and converting demand into sustainable, profitable growth entering FY27.
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: Kilburn operates six manufacturing facilities strategically aligned across India, forming an integrated manufacturing ecosystem: Saravali (Thane, Maharashtra) and Ambernath (Maharashtra) for dryers, heat exchangers, pressure vessels and heavy fabrication; Pune (M.E. Energy) for waste heat recovery, thermal systems and industrial heating; and three units at Pune (Monga Strayfield) for RF drying systems, precision manufacturing and R&D, with a commercial and assembly presence at Theale, UK. The Company has commenced expansion of the Kilburn manufacturing facility at Saravali, with completion expected within the next six to eight months; this is intended to augment production capacity and improve operational efficiency to support growing demand. During FY 2025-26 the Board approved a capital expenditure plan of approximately Rs 30 Crore for capacity expansion and cost optimisation at the Saravali, Bhiwandi facility, aimed at enhancing manufacturing capacity, improving operational efficiency and strengthening long-term growth prospects. In parallel, Phase II expansion of M.E. Energy's Pune facility has been initiated, further strengthening manufacturing scale and execution footprint. R&D capacity is anchored by a Centre of Excellence at Kilburn, Saravali equipped with seven pilot plant dryers for real-world simulation, product testing and process validation, complemented by a Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune showcasing RF technology. Inorganic expansion came through the integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, which broadened the technology platform into thermal engineering, waste heat recovery, RF heating and drying, and precision sheet metal engineering; FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of both. During the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Kilburn East End Private Limited, on 28 January 2026, which is to become a 60:40 joint venture with East End Technologies Private Limited upon completion of the transaction under the joint venture agreement dated 14 April 2026. Entering FY27, the Company reports ongoing capacity expansion initiatives alongside a healthy enquiry pipeline exceeding Rs 4,000 Crore.
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Management expects rising investments across power and energy infrastructure, nuclear power and critical infrastructure, steel and metals, mining and mineral processing, tea and agro processing, fertilisers and agrochemicals, carbon black and advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, food processing and FMCG, petrochemicals and chemicals, oil and gas, wastewater and sludge treatment, thermal energy storage, and data centres and electrical infrastructure to underpin a positive Group outlook.
- India's sustained focus on manufacturing expansion, infrastructure development, energy security, process efficiency and industrial competitiveness, alongside the realignment of global supply chains, is expected to create significant opportunities for specialised engineering and process equipment providers.
- Growing demand for energy efficiency, thermal optimisation and industrial drying technologies is a stated demand driver, with rising energy costs and decarbonisation mandates accelerating investments in waste heat recovery and thermal optimisation systems.
- The ongoing industrial capex cycle is a stated tailwind: presence across multiple process industries, a strong order pipeline and deep engineering expertise position the Company to benefit.
- Carbon black, chemicals, specialty chemicals, petrochemicals and oil & gas show strong momentum, with increasing investments in manufacturing capacity, refinery expansions and downstream petrochemical projects translating into a robust enquiry pipeline with strong conversion potential.
- The integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield creates opportunities for cross-selling across existing customer relationships, entry into new industrial segments, diversification of end markets and delivery of integrated engineering solutions.
- FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, giving a more representative view of the Group's operating scale.
- Industry structure is shifting towards sustainability, circular economy practices and process optimisation, which management expects to drive demand for integrated engineering solutions.
- A net debt-free position post fund raise, a strengthened balance sheet, expanding manufacturing capabilities, technology partnerships and a growing global footprint are cited as positioning the Group for the next phase of industrial growth.
- Management flags risks that could offset the outlook: long project execution cycles exposing the Company to input cost fluctuations and margin pressures, and industrial investment cycles, customer-led delivery deferments and payment delays affecting revenue visibility and cash flows.
- The Group ended FY26 with a healthy consolidated order book of `467 crore.
- Order inflows during the year exceeded `600 crore; the Directors' Report states total group order booking during the year was `602 Crores and total unexecuted orders as on 31st March 2026 stood at `467 Crores.
- An active enquiry pipeline exceeding `4,000 crore provides visibility for future growth; entering FY27 the Company reports a healthy enquiry pipeline exceeding `4,000 Crore.
- The Group's diversified order profile, with orders during FY26 spanning carbon black, iron and steel, petrochemicals, food processing, fertilisers, specialty applications and RF drying systems, reflects the increasing breadth of the platform.
- A robust, diversified order book supported by a steady inquiry pipeline provides revenue visibility and continuity.

currentContext.expansion: Kilburn operates six manufacturing facilities strategically aligned across India, forming an integrated manufacturing ecosystem: Saravali (Thane, Maharashtra) and Ambernath (Maharashtra) for dryers, heat exchangers, pressure vessels and heavy fabrication; Pune (M.E. Energy) for waste heat recovery, thermal systems and industrial heating; and three units at Pune (Monga Strayfield) for RF drying systems, precision manufacturing and R&D, with a commercial and assembly presence at Theale, UK. The Company has commenced expansion of the Kilburn manufacturing facility at Saravali, with completion expected within the next six to eight months; this is intended to augment production capacity and improve operational efficiency to support growing demand. During FY 2025-26 the Board approved a capital expenditure plan of approximately Rs 30 Crore for capacity expansion and cost optimisation at the Saravali, Bhiwandi facility, aimed at enhancing manufacturing capacity, improving operational efficiency and strengthening long-term growth prospects. In parallel, Phase II expansion of M.E. Energy's Pune facility has been initiated, further strengthening manufacturing scale and execution footprint. R&D capacity is anchored by a Centre of Excellence at Kilburn, Saravali equipped with seven pilot plant dryers for real-world simulation, product testing and process validation, complemented by a Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune showcasing RF technology. Inorganic expansion came through the integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, which broadened the technology platform into thermal engineering, waste heat recovery, RF heating and drying, and precision sheet metal engineering; FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of both. During the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Kilburn East End Private Limited, on 28 January 2026, which is to become a 60:40 joint venture with East End Technologies Private Limited upon completion of the transaction under the joint venture agreement dated 14 April 2026. Entering FY27, the Company reports ongoing capacity expansion initiatives alongside a healthy enquiry pipeline exceeding Rs 4,000 Crore.

risks.risk: Project execution and input cost pressure on long-cycle orders
risks.note: Long project execution cycles may expose the Company to input cost fluctuations and margin pressures. Because the business is order-backed and equipment is highly customised, a fixed-price order booked today can be delivered against materially different raw-material costs. Management relies on prudent procurement practices, vendor partnerships, commercial safeguards and close project monitoring.

risks.risk: Demand cyclicality and working capital strain
risks.note: Industrial investment cycles, customer-led delivery deferments and payment delays may impact revenue visibility and cash flows. This is structural for a capital-goods supplier whose revenue depends on customers' own capex decisions; mitigation is diversification across industries and geographies, disciplined credit management and active customer engagement.

risks.risk: Technology replication and intellectual property erosion
risks.note: The Company's differentiation rests on proprietary drying, thermal and RF process know-how. Risks arise from technology replication and evolving customer requirements, addressed through continuous investment in innovation, engineering and product development.

risks.risk: Intensifying competition from domestic and international players
risks.note: Increasing competition from domestic and international players could pressure pricing and win rates; management mitigates through proven technologies, strong execution capabilities, customised solutions and long-standing customer relationships.

risks.risk: Foreign exchange exposure from export operations
risks.note: Export operations across 50+ countries expose the Company to currency fluctuations. A structured foreign exchange risk management framework and appropriate hedging strategies are used to mitigate this exposure.

Global economic uncertainties, geopolitical developments and supply chain disruptions may affect business operations. Mitigation rests on a diversified customer base, multiple sourcing channels and robust project planning processes. The MD&A also notes global growth moderating and trade volumes projected to slow, with tariff-related uncertainties weighing on merchandise exports.

risks.risk: Integration and execution risk from recent acquisitions
risks.note: FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield. The growth thesis depends on realising cross-selling, integrated solutions and broader end-market participation from these acquisitions; the platform's scale and complexity require continued investment in engineering capability, leadership depth and project management to keep organisational capacity abreast of growth.

Although the Company serves 20+ industries, demand is uniformly tied to the industrial capex cycle across chemicals, petrochemicals, carbon black, fertilisers and metals, so a broad slowdown in process-industry investment would affect most end markets simultaneously. Diversified sectoral presence is management's stated mitigation against concentration risk.

one_liner.title: One Liner (RHP)
one_liner.body: Kilburn Engineering is a leading Indian process engineering company designing and manufacturing highly specialised drying, thermal, waste-heat-recovery and RF process equipment, with installations across 50+ countries.

business_model.title: What they do
business_model.body: The Group designs, engineers and manufactures highly specialised process equipment and systems for critical industrial applications, spanning customised industrial drying systems, packaged process systems, fabricated large critical equipment, waste heat recovery and thermal systems, Radio Frequency (RF) heating and drying, and precision manufacturing. It offers end-to-end design, manufacturing, supply, installation and commissioning, serving more than 20 industrial sectors including carbon black, chemicals, petrochemicals, fertilisers, pharmaceuticals, tea, oil & gas, nuclear power and food processing. The Group comprises Kilburn Engineering Limited with wholly owned subsidiaries M.E. Energy (thermal engineering and waste heat recovery) and Monga Strayfield (RF heating/drying and precision sheet metal).

demand_drivers.title: Demand & outlook drivers
demand_drivers.body:
- Management expects rising investments across power and energy infrastructure, nuclear power and critical infrastructure, steel and metals, mining and mineral processing, tea and agro processing, fertilisers and agrochemicals, carbon black and advanced materials, pharmaceuticals, food processing and FMCG, petrochemicals and chemicals, oil and gas, wastewater and sludge treatment, thermal energy storage, and data centres and electrical infrastructure to underpin a positive Group outlook.
- India's sustained focus on manufacturing expansion, infrastructure development, energy security, process efficiency and industrial competitiveness, alongside the realignment of global supply chains, is expected to create significant opportunities for specialised engineering and process equipment providers.
- Growing demand for energy efficiency, thermal optimisation and industrial drying technologies is a stated demand driver, with rising energy costs and decarbonisation mandates accelerating investments in waste heat recovery and thermal optimisation systems.
- The ongoing industrial capex cycle is a stated tailwind: presence across multiple process industries, a strong order pipeline and deep engineering expertise position the Company to benefit.
- Carbon black, chemicals, specialty chemicals, petrochemicals and oil & gas show strong momentum, with increasing investments in manufacturing capacity, refinery expansions and downstream petrochemical projects translating into a robust enquiry pipeline with strong conversion potential.
- The integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield creates opportunities for cross-selling across existing customer relationships, entry into new industrial segments, diversification of end markets and delivery of integrated engineering solutions.
- FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, giving a more representative view of the Group's operating scale.
- Industry structure is shifting towards sustainability, circular economy practices and process optimisation, which management expects to drive demand for integrated engineering solutions.
- A net debt-free position post fund raise, a strengthened balance sheet, expanding manufacturing capabilities, technology partnerships and a growing global footprint are cited as positioning the Group for the next phase of industrial growth.
- Management flags risks that could offset the outlook: long project execution cycles exposing the Company to input cost fluctuations and margin pressures, and industrial investment cycles, customer-led delivery deferments and payment delays affecting revenue visibility and cash flows.
- The Group ended FY26 with a healthy consolidated order book of `467 crore.
- Order inflows during the year exceeded `600 crore; the Directors' Report states total group order booking during the year was `602 Crores and total unexecuted orders as on 31st March 2026 stood at `467 Crores.
- An active enquiry pipeline exceeding `4,000 crore provides visibility for future growth; entering FY27 the Company reports a healthy enquiry pipeline exceeding `4,000 Crore.
- The Group's diversified order profile, with orders during FY26 spanning carbon black, iron and steel, petrochemicals, food processing, fertilisers, specialty applications and RF drying systems, reflects the increasing breadth of the platform.
- A robust, diversified order book supported by a steady inquiry pipeline provides revenue visibility and continuity.

capex_expansion.title: Capex & expansion plans
capex_expansion.body: Kilburn operates six manufacturing facilities strategically aligned across India, forming an integrated manufacturing ecosystem: Saravali (Thane, Maharashtra) and Ambernath (Maharashtra) for dryers, heat exchangers, pressure vessels and heavy fabrication; Pune (M.E. Energy) for waste heat recovery, thermal systems and industrial heating; and three units at Pune (Monga Strayfield) for RF drying systems, precision manufacturing and R&D, with a commercial and assembly presence at Theale, UK. The Company has commenced expansion of the Kilburn manufacturing facility at Saravali, with completion expected within the next six to eight months; this is intended to augment production capacity and improve operational efficiency to support growing demand. During FY 2025-26 the Board approved a capital expenditure plan of approximately Rs 30 Crore for capacity expansion and cost optimisation at the Saravali, Bhiwandi facility, aimed at enhancing manufacturing capacity, improving operational efficiency and strengthening long-term growth prospects. In parallel, Phase II expansion of M.E. Energy's Pune facility has been initiated, further strengthening manufacturing scale and execution footprint. R&D capacity is anchored by a Centre of Excellence at Kilburn, Saravali equipped with seven pilot plant dryers for real-world simulation, product testing and process validation, complemented by a Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune showcasing RF technology. Inorganic expansion came through the integration of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, which broadened the technology platform into thermal engineering, waste heat recovery, RF heating and drying, and precision sheet metal engineering; FY 2025-26 was the first full year of consolidation of both. During the year the Company incorporated a wholly owned subsidiary, Kilburn East End Private Limited, on 28 January 2026, which is to become a 60:40 joint venture with East End Technologies Private Limited upon completion of the transaction under the joint venture agreement dated 14 April 2026. Entering FY27, the Company reports ongoing capacity expansion initiatives alongside a healthy enquiry pipeline exceeding Rs 4,000 Crore.

management_tone.title: Management quality / tone
management_tone.body: Confident on long-term structural growth and margin sustainability (22-23%); Cautiously realistic about near-term geopolitical headwinds affecting dispatch timing; Emphasized 'high aspirations' but guided conservatively (20-25%) to manage expectations.

moat.title: Bull — competitive strengths
moat.body:
- Recognised global player in drying and process equipment with 8,000+ installations and machines worldwide across 50+ countries on six continents, giving scale and reference credibility in customised process solutions.
- Leadership position in the carbon black segment, plus a proven track record in critical oil & gas and nuclear applications including offshore skid-mounted packages and heavy water drying systems — high-specification niches with steep qualification barriers.
- Integrated technology platform combining drying, thermal and RF technologies after the acquisitions of M.E. Energy and Monga Strayfield, unlocking cross-selling and end-to-end solutions a single-technology competitor cannot offer.
- R&D moat: a Centre of Excellence at Kilburn, Saravali with seven pilot plant dryers for real-world simulation and process validation, plus a Customer Experience Centre at Monga, Pune, reducing execution risk and improving enquiry-to-order conversion.
- Global technology tie-ups with Nara Machinery (Japan), Komline Sanderson (USA) and Idreco (Switzerland), providing access to advanced technologies and alignment with global standards.
- Material versatility across aluminium, carbon steel, stainless steel, nickel, Inconel, Hastelloy, Monel, duplex stainless steel, alloy steels and titanium, enabling participation in critical, high-performance applications.
- Diversified sectoral presence across 20+ industries, which strengthens resilience and mitigates concentration risk.
- End-to-end execution capability with engineering, fabrication, assembly and testing under one roof across six manufacturing facilities, supporting turnkey and balance-of-plant delivery.
- Order-backed business model with revenue visibility from a diversified order book and an active enquiry pipeline.

strategy.title: Strategies (RHP)
strategy.body:
- Evolve over the next three to five years from a specialised drying-equipment company into a diversified industrial technology and engineering platform built on four complementary engines: process engineering, energy efficiency, advanced drying and RF technologies, and precision manufacturing.
- Keep process engineering at the core of growth by deepening application expertise and integrated engineering capabilities to address more complex requirements and deliver greater value across the project lifecycle.
- Build energy efficiency into a major growth avenue via thermal engineering and waste heat …
